Hancock County is a rural corner of north-central Iowa with Garner as its seat of government. The 2020 census counted 10,795 residents, well under the 15,402 recorded in 1940. Half the county is on the older side: the median age is 45.4, and 24.1 percent of people are 65 or over. Shrinking, aging places tend to produce a lot of dated houses that need work, and owners often discover that deferred repairs and a tax balance both stand between them and a conventional listing.

Forest City runs across the line into Winnebago County. Whichever county holds your parcel is the one that bills it, so a Forest City owner on the Winnebago side deals with a different treasurer entirely. Look at the parcel location on your tax statement before picking up the phone.

sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Payments go to the Hancock County Treasurer, based in the Courthouse at 855 State Street, Garner, IA 50438. Walk-in hours run 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, with holidays off. The number is 641-923-3122. Anything about how your house was valued, or whether you qualify for an exemption, belongs with the assessor's office down the hall of the same government, not the treasurer.

The county offers credits for elderly and disabled owners. Dollar limits get revised, so ask the office for today's figures before you plan around one.

• Fall installment: due September 1, delinquent October 1.
  • Spring installment: due March 1, delinquent April 1.
  • A single full-year payment is accepted in September.
  • A delinquency notice goes out on November 1 and again on May 1.
  • At the counter, a debit card adds $2.00 and a credit card adds 2.25 percent. Online, an eCheck runs $0.25, and cards carry those same charges.

Interest on a late installment is 1.5 percent per month, counted from the first day after delinquency. Not getting a statement is no defense. State rules make the owner responsible for seeing that a bill arrives, so if nothing has shown up by late summer, phone the treasurer rather than wait.

An owner who thinks the assessed value is off can file a written protest with the Board of Review from April 2 through April 30. Hancock's board has five members and sits on or about May 1, and it owes you a written decision that explains its reasoning.

Iowa Code 441.37 limits you to specific complaints. Pick the one that fits:

  • Similar property is valued lower, so yours is out of line.
  • The figure is higher than the law permits.
  • The classification is wrong, or the parcel should be exempt.
  • Someone made a mistake in the assessment.
  • Fraud was involved.

A bare statement that the number seems high rarely succeeds. Gather values for a few comparable houses close to yours and submit them with the protest.

The old homestead credit is being replaced by a homestead exemption equal to 10 percent of taxable value, floored at $5,500 and capped at $20,000. It begins with assessment year 2026. Owners 65 and older who want the 65-plus exemption must file a fresh application with the assessor, even when a credit was already attached to the property.

Rollback is the state's yearly adjustment that keeps taxable value growth to 3 percent across Iowa. The Iowa Taxpayers Research foundation illustrated it with a 2025 residential rollback of 44.5345 percent. Local levy rates are outside that limit, which is why a bill can climb in a year when rollback looks favorable.

Each year on the third Monday of June at 9:00 a.m., the county auctions delinquent parcels online. Bidders sign up at iowataxauction.com. Iowa Code chapter 446 requires the treasurer to put these parcels up for sale.

  • Around June 1 the parcel list is posted, and it is refreshed daily until the auction.
  • The June newspaper ad names the delinquent owners, and the publication fee lands on May 1 whether or not you pay later.
  • A sale notice must be mailed by May 1 addressed to the name on the tax record.
  • The last day to pay and avoid being published shifts annually. Get the current cutoff from the treasurer.
  • To redeem a sold parcel you need guaranteed funds, and interest runs 2 percent each month.

Owners who are behind should act before the list goes up. Closing a sale first means the balance is settled from what you receive, rather than redeemed later at 2 percent a month.

Property tax trails the calendar by a year. At closing it is either split between the parties or the seller pays the treasurer separately. If the house sells from July 1 through December 31, the September installment is the seller's problem. If it sells from January 1 through June 30, the March installment is. Any back taxes come out of the sale proceeds so the new owner gets a clean title.

Expect the state's transfer tax too: 80 cents per $500 of value after the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). You file a declaration of value with the county recorder along with the deed. The recorder passes a copy to the assessor, who holds it for three years counted from December 31 of the year of transfer.

Before you list, collect your last two tax statements, any notice from the treasurer and the names of everyone on the title. The closing agent will ask for all of it.

Hancock County winters punish roofs, furnaces and plumbing. Forest City averages about 40.2 inches of snow a year. When a buyer's inspector walks an older farm-town house, the usual flags are the roof, insulation, the heating system and a damp basement. Financed buyers commonly ask the seller to repair these or lower the price.

An as-is cash purchase skips that negotiation. Liens, back taxes and open permits do not disappear, though. They are cleared at the closing table whichever way the house sells, so find out what is attached to your parcel early, and the sale will move faster.

faqs.q: When are Hancock County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The fall installment is due September 1 and delinquent October 1. The spring installment is due March 1 and delinquent April 1. You may also pay the whole year in September.

faqs.q: Where is the Hancock County Treasurer?
faqs.a: The office is in the Courthouse at 855 State Street, Garner, Iowa 50438. It is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone number is 641-923-3122.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to redeem a Hancock County tax sale parcel?
faqs.a: You pay the price the parcel sold for plus 2 percent interest for each month, using guaranteed funds. Ask the treasurer for an exact payoff figure.

faqs.q: Is Forest City in Hancock County?
faqs.a: Partly. The city spans Hancock and Winnebago counties, and the county containing your parcel decides which treasurer sends the bill.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest my Hancock County assessment?
faqs.a: The written protest goes to the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30. The board meets on or about May 1 and must answer in writing.
